existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Hourly labor charge capped at lowest-paid qualified employee's salary
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: An agency may impose a reasonable charge for search, retrieval, and redaction, but that charge shall not exceed the prorated hourly salary of the lowest paid full-time employee who, in the custodian's reasonable discretion, has the necessary skill and training to perform the request.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Agency performs search, retrieval, or redaction
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: In all other instances, the charge for the search, retrieval, or redaction of records shall not exceed the prorated hourly salary of the lowest paid full-time employee who, in the reasonable discretion of the custodian of the records, has the necessary skill and training to perform the request; provided, however, that no charge shall be made for the first quarter hour.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Ceiling basis: state caps the rate at the lowest-paid qualified employee's prorated salary; city supplies the actual dollar figure. Confirmed unchanged in 2024 Georgia Code. Verbatim.

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: First quarter hour of labor is free
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: No labor charge may be made for the first quarter hour of search, retrieval, or redaction.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: provided, however, that no charge shall be made for the first quarter hour.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Fixed statutory free increment of 15 minutes. Verbatim.

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Copy charge capped at 10 cents per page
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: In addition to labor charges, an agency may charge for copying, not to exceed 10 cents per page for letter or legal size documents, or the actual cost of producing the copy for other document types.
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: In addition to a charge for the search, retrieval, or redaction of records, an agency may charge a fee for the copying of records or data, not to exceed 10¢ per page for letter or legal size documents or, in the case of other documents, the actual cost of producing the copy.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Ceiling of $0.25... note: ceiling is $0.10/page for letter/legal; other sizes at actual cost. City supplies the operative per-page value under the cap. Confirmed unchanged in 2024 Georgia Code. Verbatim.

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Electronic records charged at actual cost of media
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: For electronic records, the agency may charge the actual cost of the media on which the records or data are produced.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Agency produces records on electronic media
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: In the case of electronic records, the agency may charge the actual cost of the media on which the records or data are produced.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Basis is actual cost of media (a fixed measured cost, not a discretionary rate). Verbatim.

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Specific statutory fees supersede the general fee scheme
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: Where a specific fee for certified copies or other records is authorized or prescribed by law, that specific fee applies instead of the general search/retrieval/copy charges when such records are sought.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Requested record is one for which a specific statutory fee is prescribed (e.g., certified copies)
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: Where fees for certified copies or other copies or records are specifically authorized or otherwise prescribed by law, such specific fee shall apply when certified copies or other records to which a specific fee may apply are sought.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Routes certain record types to a different fee basis; branch, not a value. Verbatim.

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Cost estimate notice when costs will exceed $25
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: Where an agency will seek costs in excess of $25.00 to respond, it shall notify the requester within three business days and inform the requester of the cost estimate.
existing_fee_payment_rules.clock_spec: estimate notice due within 3 business-days of receipt of request
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: In any instance in which an agency will seek costs in excess of $25.00 for responding to a request, the agency shall notify the requester within a reasonable amount of time not to exceed three business days and inform the requester of the estimate of the costs, and the agency may defer search and retrieval of the records until the requester agrees to pay the estimated costs unless the requester has stated in his or her request a willingness to pay an amount that exceeds the search and retrieval costs.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. The $25.00 threshold is fixed by statute (city cannot change it), so it is a structural trigger, not a city-filled parameter. This row is the estimate-notice duty; GA-0023 splits out the deferral permission the same sentence carries. Confirmed unchanged in 2024 Georgia Code. Verbatim.

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Deferral of search/retrieval until requester agrees to pay estimate
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: The agency may defer search and retrieval until the requester agrees to pay the estimated costs, unless the request already stated a willingness to pay an amount exceeding the search and retrieval costs.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Cost estimate issued under GA-0022 and requester has not pre-committed to pay
existing_fee_payment_rules.clock_spec: processing paused until requester agrees to pay the estimated costs
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: and the agency may defer search and retrieval of the records until the requester agrees to pay the estimated costs unless the requester has stated in his or her request a willingness to pay an amount that exceeds the search and retrieval costs.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Verbatim. A pause state pending cost agreement; the pre-commitment carve-out prevents the pause.

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Prepayment may be required when estimate exceeds $500
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: Where the estimated production cost exceeds $500.00, the agency may insist on prepayment of the costs before beginning search, retrieval, review, or production.
existing_fee_payment_rules.clock_spec: processing paused pending prepayment when estimate exceeds $500.00
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: In any instance in which the estimated costs for production of the records exceeds $500.00, an agency may insist on prepayment of the costs prior to beginning search, retrieval, review, or production of the records.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. The $500.00 threshold is fixed by statute; structural trigger. Confirmed unchanged in 2024 Georgia Code. Verbatim.

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Prepayment for future requests where prior costs unpaid
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: Where a requester has not paid costs lawfully incurred for a prior request, the agency may require prepayment for all future requests from that person until the prior costs are paid or the payment dispute is resolved.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Requester has unpaid lawfully-incurred costs from a prior request
existing_fee_payment_rules.clock_spec: future requests paused pending prepayment until prior costs paid or dispute resolved
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: Whenever any person who has requested to inspect or copy a public record has not paid the cost for search, retrieval, redaction, or copying of such records when such charges have been lawfully incurred, an agency may require prepayment for compliance with all future requests for production of records from that person until the costs for the prior production of records have been paid or the dispute regarding payment resolved.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Verbatim. Requester-level state (delinquent) that gates future requests.

existing_fee_payment_rules.legal_concept: Collection of agreed costs regardless of whether records are accepted
existing_fee_payment_rules.atomic_rule: Where charges were lawfully estimated and agreed and the agency has incurred the agreed-upon costs to make records available, the agency may collect those charges (via tax/fee collection methods) regardless of whether the requester inspects or accepts the records.
existing_fee_payment_rules.trigger: Requester agreed to estimated costs, agency incurred them, and requester does not pay
existing_fee_payment_rules.source_language: Whenever any person has requested to inspect or copy a public record and does not pay the cost for search, retrieval, redaction, or copying of such records when such charges have been lawfully estimated and agreed to pursuant to this article, and the agency has incurred the agreed-upon costs to make the records available, regardless of whether the requester inspects or accepts copies of the records, the agency shall be authorized to collect such charges in any manner authorized by law for the collection of taxes, fees, or assessments by such agency.
existing_fee_payment_rules.notes: Source Type: Statute. Verbatim. Affects billing/collection state of a request; included as a processing permission rather than a pure damages remedy.
